clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old African American male presented with progressive abdominal distention, early satiety, and left-sided flank pain over one year. Physical examination revealed a large left flank mass with abdominal distention. Initial imaging was suspicious for giant renal angiomyolipoma (AML), but MRI eight months into presentation showed a 20 x 18.6 x 22.2 cm left retroperitoneal fat-containing mass compressing the inferior vena cava, with radiology suggesting liposarcoma in the differential diagnosis. Surgical resection with radical left nephrectomy and 2 cm surgical margins was performed. Histopathologic examination confirmed well-differentiated liposarcoma (WDL) histologic grade 1, with H&E microscopy showing variably sized mature adipocytes with bands of fibrotic stroma containing spindle cells with enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei. The tumor abutted but did not invade adjacent kidney tissue. Post-operative course was uncomplicated with discharge on post-operative day 5, and the patient was recovering well at one-week follow-up.
